messages:
Noah: hey team — first day. trying to access the app-team namespace but keep getting 403s after using Teleport. did `tsh login` + `tsh kube login --cluster=redwood` and set KUBECONFIG=/tmp/kube, but `kubectl get pods -n app-team` -> Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden... anyone seen this?

Luca: welcome! @Noah — quick q: did you use the cluster name exactly `redwood`? also, Teleport maps users to roles/groups. you probably need an RBAC binding for the teleport role.

Noah: yes cluster is `redwood`. full error: `Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User "teleport:user/noah" cannot list resource "pods" in API group "" in the namespace "app-team"`

DevEx: @Noah fwiw new hires normally get `devs-onboarding` group for week 1 which is bound to `app-team` in staging. looks like you didn't get that binding. can you run these and paste results?
`kubectl auth can-i list pods -n app-team --as=teleport:user/noah`
`kubectl config view --minify`

Noah: running: 
`$ kubectl auth can-i list pods -n app-team --as=teleport:user/noah`
`no`

`kubectl config view --minify` shows a single context: `teleport/redwood` and user `teleport:user/noah`. no namespace set.

Jamie: @DevEx @Luca fyi — onboarding binder didn't run for Noah (race in provisioning). I can create a temporary RoleBinding to `teleport:role:devs` or add him to `devs-onboarding`. which do you prefer?

DevEx: temp RoleBinding is fine. note: prefer adding to `devs-onboarding` group so CI and other perms align. Jamie can add that. @Noah — once added, run `tsh kube login --cluster=redwood --ttl=1h` again and `kubectl config use-context teleport/redwood` (or set namespace with `kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=app-team`).

teleport-bot: Teleport: role assignment for user/noah updated (audit id: t-8a3f).

Noah: thanks! after Jamie's change and re-login `kubectl get pods -n app-team` works now. one more q: is it normal that my kubeconfig path is in /tmp? should I export to ~/.kube/config instead?

Luca: for Teleport we recommend keeping the generated kubeconfig separate (eg ~/.kube/teleport-noah) and use `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/teleport-noah:~/.kube/config` in your shell rc or use `kubectl config view --flatten > ~/.kube/config` if you want a merged file. avoid overwriting default unless you know what you're doing.

DevEx: Also filing a short onboarding checklist issue so we don't miss the binder step: https://go/redwood/infra-onboard (internal). :memo:

Noah: perfect — appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:
